notes.text: The opening identifies script X as an amalgamated sum of barred W and the disjoint union of barred U_i, over the disjoint union of B_i. A second display identifies it with a coproduct of X_i, with an uncertain parenthesized w/W index; the side display relates an uncertain X_{w/i} to script X_i and Im X_i, glossed as open in script X. The three-lobed sketch has six transverse marks and a narrow return loop. The page does not define the full gluing data, so these assertions were carried without a universal-property proof.

The map script X to X is stated to be étale away from the coproduct of C_i and an “imm fermée” at its points. The abbreviation is preserved. The prose connective is “c’est une”, not H’s “i.e.”; no local geometric proof is supplied here.

Item 6 proposes an “Énoncé d’invariance” under replacement of K by K-star, with replacement formulas and edited conditions. The slanted note is “vérifier l’énoncé précis...”. The two tiny superscripts in the interlinear primed-U equation remain wedge/star, with wedge first on visual grounds; larger stars are unchanged. The crossed K condition and crossed K-like group remain uncertain. The live sufficient condition reads int K-prime containing the union of C_i, agreeing with H against C’s soit. The dotted i and final t, not mathematical expectation, decide this word. The unclosed parenthesis and live prime are retained; invariance and sufficiency are not proved.

The final question is “vérifier si dans les div. hypothèses précédentes, il n’y avait pas lieu d’exiger” union C_i subset int K, followed by the i.e. condition C_i intersect dotted K empty for every i in I. The main reader checked only the conditional set-theoretic equivalence: if K is closed, each C_i lies in K, and dotted K denotes its frontier, then frontier K = K minus int K, hence the two stated conditions are equivalent. This does not establish the missing standing assumptions, the earlier hypotheses, or the proposed invariance. The author’s own page numeral is 5; the separate archive 5 remains a comment.
